chapter: Publishing, Jelly Roll in Los Angeles and band lore
title: Dances of the era: Texas Tommy, Ballin' the Jack and the shimmy
summary: Texas Tommy began in San Francisco around 1910-12, Ballin' the Jack came in 1916 and the shimmy about 1920.

story.theme_name: Playing for dancers: dance bands and the dances themselves
story.community_name: Dancing to the band: quadrilles, waltzes and dance sets

blocks.x: Okay, got that straight. And, oh, you were mentioning when you were working, I think, in San Francisco, a dance evolved there called the "Texas Tommy"? Is that right? It started in San Francisco?
What were some of the other dances around that time?

Oh, that was the big one. That was about it. It was popular like it was a... 'Course, right after that "Texas Tommy," then the "Ballin' The Jack" came out. "Ballin' the Jack" came out '16, "Texas Tommy" come out '10, '11 or '12. It was a fast dance, you know.

You go fast as you could. They done all that stuff that, you know, that you throw your partner and twist her around and catch her and all but in a real fast [sings syllables to indicate tempo of dance]--da-de-tuh-tuh-ti-tuh-tuh-tuh-tuh-ti-tuh--just as fast as he could play it. Yeah...and that ...but it was mostly guys that done it was exhibition dancers, you know.
It wasn't something that people just did when they went out to dance.

No, no. No, even "Ballin' the Jack" that people didn't do that much--only kids and things. You know "Ballin' the Jack," don't you? [Sings]"Place two fingers"[hums], then you get down, you do the "Ballin' the Jack," you do it to the right and you do it to the left. This dance come out that ever'body was doin' was about in '20 called "Shimmy Shewahoo."
"Shimmy Shewahoo." Like when..... and they played it "I Wish I Could Shimmy Like My Sister Kate." Well, that...you...dance... you just walk along and shake all the time.
